title: Ops Exchange Scratchpad — SLO FastLabs & Micro-experiments
content:
Context:
This is a working scratchpad to coordinate a set of small, short-lived SLO calibration experiments we can run across product, hosting, and infra teams. Goal is not to redesign SLOs end-to-end — its to build a repeatable micro-experiment cadence (FastLabs) that surfaces signal quickly and gives teams confidence to iterate.

Audience: eng-sre, platform-engineering, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, observability team leads, oncall reps.

Why this exists (short):
- Weve got SLOs that are broadly useful but brittle when traffic patterns shift (batchy spikes, cache warmup, quantized model rollouts).
- Full SLO rework is slow; we want lightweight experiments to test hypotheses: e.g., prefix-cache hit thresholds, short-window latency SLOs, backoff/queueing effects under bursty traffic.
- Build common templates and runbook fragments so feature teams can run their own FastLabs.

Primary goals for the next 8 weeks:
- Ship 6 micro-experiments (1–2 week duration) across 3 services.
- Produce a concise result card for each experiment with measured signal, recommended action (none / tweak / adopt / rollback), and confidence level.
- Create a one-page FastLabs template and a minimal runbook fragment that integrates with oncall rotation.

Success metrics (how well know this is useful):
- 6 experiment result cards published to the SRE FastLabs folder.
- At least 2 teams adopt a recommended SLO tweak within 4 weeks of experiment close.
- Experiment templates used by at least 3 distinct feature teams (tracked via tags/Jira links).

Scope (whats in/out):
- In: latency SLO micro-calibrations, short-window (1m/5m) error-rate probes, prefix cache hit experiments, graceful degradation policy tests (fallback model variants).
- Out: full SLO policy rewrite, infra budget changes, legal/security compliance work (these will be flagged and handed off).

FastLabs experiment template (use this for every run):
- Name: short slug (e.g., prefix-cache-hit-1m).
- Owner: one primary person.
- Duration: 7–14 days.
- Hypothesis: one line.
- Signal: list of 2–4 metrics (p50/95/99 latency, error-rate, cache hit%, token/sec).
- Success criteria: numeric threshold + direction (e.g., p95 decreases >15% with <2% error delta).
- Safety checks: commit to rollback criteria (error spike > X, user-impact alert).
- Stakeholders: product, infra, observability, oncall.
- Tickets/links: Jira keys + dashboards.

Experiment matrix (initial candidates):
1) prefix-cache-hit-1m (serving-runtime): Hypothesis: enabling 1-minute prefix caching increases p95 token latency for short prompts by 20% reduction under bursty traffic. Duration 10d. Owner: Jonah. Safety: rollback if error-rate rises >1.5x baseline. Linked to JIRA-2201.
2) short-window-latency-SLO (hosted-api): Hypothesis: adding a p99 1-minute SLO reduces tail latency regressions for interactive features; test whether alert noise increases. Duration 14d. Owner: Priya. Safety: pause if alert volume > 3x baseline/shift. JIRA-2199.
3) fallback-model-rollout-traffic-shift (dedicated): Hypothesis: automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized model under overload maintains success rate while lowering cost; test routing and quality degradation. Duration 14d. Owner: Diego. Safety: abort if human-quality-eval fails threshold. Linked to evaluation harness in GIT-PR-345.
4) queueing-backpressure-alpha (platform-engineering): Hypothesis: adding mild request queuing and 50ms token batching keeps latency SLO but reduces downstream overload events. Duration 7d. Owner: Carmen. Safety: abort if upstream timeouts > baseline + 2%. JIRA-2215.
5) synthetic-slo-sensitivity (observability): short synthetic traffic spikes to measure SLO sensitivity window. Owner: Maya. Duration 7d. Safety: ensure synthetic runs do not saturate region capacity; coordinate with infra.
6) cross-service-degradation-cascade (oncall pairing): tabletop + lightweight chaos experiments to enumerate hidden dependencies and ensure runbooks exist. Owner: rotating oncall rep. Duration 7d.

Runbook fragment (minimal to attach to each experiment):
- Pre-run checklist: runbook owner identified, dashboard links created (p50/p95/p99, errors, throughput), rollback channel (#sre-fastlabs), blast radius estimate, stakeholders paged.
- During-run: daily short update (3 bullets) in the experiment thread, oncall has explicit abort permission.
- Post-run: result card + 30-minute readout; record whether experiment produced actionable change.

Communication & stakeholder cadence:
- Kickoff huddle (30m) for each experiment with product + infra + obs.
- Daily asynchronous updates in thread (one-line status).
- Mid-run checkpoint (optional) if metrics trending close to thresholds.
- 30-minute readout + decision (adopt / tweak / no-change / deeper investigation).

Roles & responsibilities (suggested):
- Experiment owner: run the test, own Jira ticket, write result card.
- SRE sponsor: ensure safety checks, review dashboards, coordinate rollback.
- Observability: instrument dashboards, add alert filters for experiment traffic.
- Product lead: sign-off on user-impact acceptance criteria.
- Oncall rep: empowered to abort and execute rollback runbook.

Tooling notes (quick list):
- Dashboards: create a minimal Grafana panel with p50/p95/p99 + errors + traffic split.
- Tagging: add tag fastlabs=experiment-name to traces/metrics where possible to filter noise.
- Traffic shaping: use platform-engineering test routing to direct 5–10% of traffic for safe experiments.
- Evals: attach small human evaluation checklists for model-quality experiments (link to GH evaluation notebook).

Example result card template (one paragraph + 4 bullets):
- Summary: one-line.
- Metrics: before/after numbers.
- Decision: adopt/tweak/no-change/rollback.
- Confidence & next steps: short.

Open questions / things to resolve quickly:
- Can we safely tag 5% of production traffic for experiments without breaking telemetry billing? (action: finance and infra to confirm)
- Quick method to run human-evals at small scale for model rollbacks (action: research/solutions to provide harness).
- Who updates the canonical SLO doc if a FastLabs outcome leads to permanent change? (suggestion: product-hosted-api owner + SRE sponsor).

Risks and mitigations:
- Alert fatigue: minimal SLO changes only; prefer short-window experiments vs permanent alert changes. Mitigation: observability to add experiment filter for alerts.
- Customer impact: limit traffic percentage, explicit rollback thresholds, and oncall abort authority.
- Cross-team coordination overhead: keep experiments small (<=2 weeks), provide a one-pager template to reduce kickoff time.

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Finalize owners for experiments 1,2,3 by EOD Friday (action: Maya to ping leads).
- Create Jira tickets for each experiment and link dashboards (action: Jonah).
- Schedule a FastLabs kickoff rotation (bi-weekly 30m slot) to triage proposals (action: Priya).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small badge in console for feature teams that have run a FastLab and adopted results (motivation).
- Keep a small "FastLabs hall of fame" with 1-page writeups that product folks can read in 3 mins.

History/traces: this doc is intentionally lightweight; its a coordination scratchpad, expect to transcribe outcome cards and move final summaries to Confluence.

If youre reading and want to run a micro-experiment: add a single-line proposal below with owner and one metric.

-- Maya
